claim: GOT2 is part of the malate-aspartate shuttle, a mechanism by which cells transfer reducing equivalents from the cytosol to the mitochondria.
source: Mitochondrial glutamate-oxaloacetate transaminase 2 (GOT2) is part of the malate-aspartate shuttle, a mechanism by which cells transfer reducing equivalents from the cytosol to the mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is established scientific knowledge about GOT2's function.

claim: GOT2 is a key component of mutant KRAS-mediated rewiring of glutamine metabolism in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
source: GOT2 is a key component of mutant KRAS (KRAS*)-mediated rewiring of glutamine metabolism in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and is supported by prior work from the authors' lab.

claim: Loss of GOT2 disturbs redox homeostasis in PDA cells in vitro.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the loss of GOT2 disturbs redox homeostasis and halts proliferation of PDA cells in vitro.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Loss of GOT2 halts proliferation of PDA cells in vitro.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the loss of GOT2 disturbs redox homeostasis and halts proliferation of PDA cells in vitro.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by colony formation and proliferation assays.

claim: GOT2 knockdown in PDA cell lines in vitro induced NADH accumulation.
source: GOT2 knockdown (KD) in PDA cell lines in vitro induced NADH accumulation, decreased Asp and α-ketoglutarate (αKG) production, stalled glycolysis, disrupted the TCA cycle, and impaired proliferation.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by metabolomics data showing increased NADH/NAD+ ratio.

claim: GOT2 knockdown decreased aspartate production in PDA cell lines in vitro.
source: GOT2 knockdown (KD) in PDA cell lines in vitro induced NADH accumulation, decreased Asp and α-ketoglutarate (αKG) production, stalled glycolysis, disrupted the TCA cycle, and impaired proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by metabolomics data in Figure 1E.

claim: GOT2 knockdown decreased α-ketoglutarate production in PDA cell lines in vitro.
source: GOT2 knockdown (KD) in PDA cell lines in vitro induced NADH accumulation, decreased Asp and α-ketoglutarate (αKG) production, stalled glycolysis, disrupted the TCA cycle, and impaired proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by metabolomics data in Figure 1E.

claim: GOT2 knockdown stalled glycolysis in PDA cell lines in vitro.
source: GOT2 knockdown (KD) in PDA cell lines in vitro induced NADH accumulation, decreased Asp and α-ketoglutarate (αKG) production, stalled glycolysis, disrupted the TCA cycle, and impaired proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by metabolomics data showing glycolytic metabolite changes and Seahorse glycolytic rate assays.

claim: GOT2 knockdown disrupted the TCA cycle in PDA cell lines in vitro.
source: GOT2 knockdown (KD) in PDA cell lines in vitro induced NADH accumulation, decreased Asp and α-ketoglutarate (αKG) production, stalled glycolysis, disrupted the TCA cycle, and impaired proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by metabolomics data showing changes in TCA cycle intermediates.

claim: Oxidizing NADH through chemical or genetic means resolved the redox imbalance induced by GOT2 KD.
source: Oxidizing NADH through chemical or genetic means resolved the redox imbalance induced by GOT2 KD, permitting sustained proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using pyruvate, α-ketobutyrate, and LbNOX expression.

claim: Oxidizing NADH permitted sustained proliferation in GOT2 KD cells.
source: Oxidizing NADH through chemical or genetic means resolved the redox imbalance induced by GOT2 KD, permitting sustained proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by proliferation assays with pyruvate supplementation and LbNOX expression.

claim: Loss of GOT2 had no effect on tumor growth in xenograft PDA models.
source: Despite a strong in vitro inhibitory phenotype, loss of GOT2 had no effect on tumor growth in xenograft PDA or autochthonous mouse models.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by tumor volume measurements in NSG mice.

claim: Loss of GOT2 had no effect on tumor growth in autochthonous mouse models.
source: Despite a strong in vitro inhibitory phenotype, loss of GOT2 had no effect on tumor growth in xenograft PDA or autochthonous mouse models.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data from KC-Got2 mouse model experiments.

claim: Cancer-associated fibroblasts release the redox active metabolite pyruvate.
source: We show that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), a major component of the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), release the redox active metabolite pyruvate, and culturing GOT2 KD cells in CAF conditioned media (CM) rescued proliferation in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by metabolomics analysis of CAF conditioned media and isotope tracing experiments.

claim: Culturing GOT2 KD cells in CAF conditioned media rescued proliferation in vitro.
source: We show that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), a major component of the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), release the redox active metabolite pyruvate, and culturing GOT2 KD cells in CAF conditioned media (CM) rescued proliferation in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by colony formation and proliferation assays with CAF CM.

claim: Blocking pyruvate import prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by exogenous pyruvate.
source: Furthermore, blocking pyruvate import or pyruvate-to-lactate reduction prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by exogenous pyruvate or CAF CM.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using MCT1 inhibition and knockout.

claim: Blocking pyruvate-to-lactate reduction prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by exogenous pyruvate.
source: Furthermore, blocking pyruvate import or pyruvate-to-lactate reduction prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by exogenous pyruvate or CAF CM.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using LDHA inhibitor FX11.

claim: Blocking pyruvate import prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by CAF CM.
source: Furthermore, blocking pyruvate import or pyruvate-to-lactate reduction prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by exogenous pyruvate or CAF CM.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using MCT1 inhibition with CAF CM.

claim: Blocking pyruvate-to-lactate reduction prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by CAF CM.
source: Furthermore, blocking pyruvate import or pyruvate-to-lactate reduction prevented rescue of GOT2 KD in vitro by exogenous pyruvate or CAF CM.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments using LDHA inhibitor FX11 with CAF CM.

claim: Blocking pyruvate import or metabolism failed to sensitize xenografts to GOT2 KD in vivo.
source: However, these interventions failed to sensitize xenografts to GOT2 KD in vivo, demonstrating the remarkable plasticity and differential metabolism deployed by PDA cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vivo experiments with MCT1 inhibition/knockout and LDHA inhibition.

claim: PDA cells demonstrate remarkable plasticity and differential metabolism in vitro versus in vivo.
source: However, these interventions failed to sensitize xenografts to GOT2 KD in vivo, demonstrating the remarkable plasticity and differential metabolism deployed by PDA cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the abstract based on the differential effects of GOT2 KD in vitro versus in vivo.

claim: Cancer cells depend on deregulated metabolic programs to meet energetic and biosynthetic demands.
source: Cancer cells depend on deregulated metabolic programs to meet energetic and biosynthetic demands (Pavlova and Thompson, 2016; Vander Heiden and DeBerardinis, 2017; Martínez-Reyes and Chandel, 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations to established literature.

claim: Metabolic therapies aim to preferentially target cancer cell metabolic dependencies.
source: Metabolic therapies aim to preferentially target these dependencies (Vander Heiden, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Metabolic therapy has shown promise in preclinical models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
source: This approach has shown promise in preclinical models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA) – one of the deadliest major cancers, notoriously resistant to anti-cancer therapies (Ryan et al., 2014; Halbrook and Lyssiotis, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: PDA is one of the deadliest major cancers.
source: This approach has shown promise in preclinical models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA) – one of the deadliest major cancers, notoriously resistant to anti-cancer therapies (Ryan et al., 2014; Halbrook and Lyssiotis, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge about PDA.

claim: PDA is notoriously resistant to anti-cancer therapies.
source: This approach has shown promise in preclinical models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA) – one of the deadliest major cancers, notoriously resistant to anti-cancer therapies (Ryan et al., 2014; Halbrook and Lyssiotis, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Pancreatic tumors are poorly vascularized.
source: Pancreatic tumors are poorly vascularized and nutrient dysregulated (Kamphorst et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Pancreatic tumors are nutrient dysregulated.
source: Pancreatic tumors are poorly vascularized and nutrient dysregulated (Kamphorst et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Cancer cells commandeer metabolic pathways to scavenge and use nutrients.
source: Therefore, cancer cells commandeer metabolic pathways to scavenge and use nutrients (Halbrook and Lyssiotis, 2017; Encarnación-Rosado and Kimmelman, 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Metabolic rewiring in pancreatic cancer is mediated predominantly by mutant KRAS.
source: A wealth of recent literature has identified that this is mediated predominantly by mutant KRAS (KRAS*), the oncogenic driver in most pancreatic tumors (Commisso et al., 2013; Ying et al., 2012; Son et al., 2013; Viale et al., 2014; Santana-Codina et al., 2018; Humpton et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Mutant KRAS is the oncogenic driver in most pancreatic tumors.
source: A wealth of recent literature has identified that this is mediated predominantly by mutant KRAS (KRAS*), the oncogenic driver in most pancreatic tumors (Commisso et al., 2013; Ying et al., 2012; Son et al., 2013; Viale et al., 2014; Santana-Codina et al., 2018; Humpton et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Mutant KRAS has been implicated in shaping the pancreatic tumor microenvironment.
source: The KRAS* has also been implicated in shaping the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME; Tape et al., 2016; Kerk et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: PDA tumors exhibit a complex tumor microenvironment.
source: The PDA tumors exhibit a complex TME (Storz and Crawford, 2020; Zhang et al., 2019) with metabolic interactions between malignant, stromal, and immune cells enabling and facilitating tumor progression (Lyssiotis and Kimmelman, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Metabolic interactions between malignant, stromal, and immune cells enable and facilitate tumor progression in PDA.
source: The PDA tumors exhibit a complex TME (Storz and Crawford, 2020; Zhang et al., 2019) with metabolic interactions between malignant, stromal, and immune cells enabling and facilitating tumor progression (Lyssiotis and Kimmelman, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: KRAS-selective inhibitors are in various stages of preclinical and clinical testing.
source: Recent successes in drug development have provided KRAS* selective inhibitors, and these are in various stages of preclinical and clinical testing.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and reflects current knowledge of KRAS inhibitor development.

claim: Resistance to KRAS-selective inhibitors inevitably occurs.
source: However, consistent with other targeted therapies, resistance inevitably occurs (Janes et al., 2018; Jänne, 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Disrupting downstream metabolic crosstalk mechanisms in PDA is a compelling combinatorial or alternative approach to KRAS inhibition.
source: Therefore, disrupting downstream metabolic crosstalk mechanisms in PDA is a compelling combinatorial or alternative approach (Cox et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a rationale for the study and supported by citation.

claim: PDA cells are uniquely dependent on KRAS-mediated rewiring of glutamine metabolism for protection against oxidative stress.
source: In support of this idea, previous work from our lab described that PDA cells are uniquely dependent on KRAS*-mediated rewiring of glutamine metabolism for protection against oxidative stress (Son et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to prior work from the authors' lab.

claim: GOT2 is implicated in KRAS-mediated rewired metabolism in PDA.
source: Mitochondrial glutamate-oxaloacetate transaminase 2 (GOT2) is implicated in this rewired metabolism in PDA.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on prior work.

claim: GOT2 functions in the malate-aspartate shuttle in normal physiology.
source: In normal physiology, GOT2 functions in the malate-aspartate shuttle (MAS), a mechanism by which cells transfer reducing equivalents between the cytosol and mitochondria to balance the two independent NADH pools and maintain redox balance (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1A, representing established knowledge.

claim: The malate-aspartate shuttle is a mechanism by which cells transfer reducing equivalents between the cytosol and mitochondria to balance NADH pools and maintain redox balance.
source: In normal physiology, GOT2 functions in the malate-aspartate shuttle (MAS), a mechanism by which cells transfer reducing equivalents between the cytosol and mitochondria to balance the two independent NADH pools and maintain redox balance (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1A, representing established knowledge.

claim: PDA cells driven by mutant KRAS divert metabolites from the MAS and increase flux through malic enzyme 1 to produce NADPH.
source: The PDA cells driven by KRAS* divert metabolites from the MAS and increase flux through malic enzyme 1 (ME1) to produce NADPH (Son et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Loss of GOT2 in vitro induces intracellular NADH accumulation and reductive stress.
source: Using metabolomics analyses and manipulation of the redox state in PDA cells, we discovered that loss of GOT2 in vitro induces intracellular NADH accumulation and reductive stress.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a key finding and supported by metabolomics data.

claim: Metabolic changes from GOT2 loss impair cellular growth, which can be rescued with chemical or genetic interventions that oxidize NADH.
source: These metabolic changes impair cellular growth, which can be rescued with chemical or genetic interventions that oxidize NADH.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a key finding and supported by rescue experiments with pyruvate and LbNOX.

claim: Cancer cells use complex cell-intrinsic rewiring and crosstalk with the TME to maintain redox homeostasis in vivo.
source: Cancer cells use a complex cell-intrinsic rewiring and crosstalk with the TME to maintain redox homeostasis in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Doxycycline induction of shGOT2 in PaTu-8902 cells decreased GOT2 protein expression.
source: Immunoblot of GOT2 and VINCULIN loading control in PaTu-8902 cells after 1 µg/mL doxycycline (DOX) induction of two independent GOT2 (sh1, sh2) and non-targeting (NT) shRNAs for 3 days.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B with western blot data.

claim: GOT2 knockdown impaired colony formation in PDA cells.
source: Representative images from colony formation assays in ishRNA PaTu-8902 cells −Dox (n=3) or +Dox (n=3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C and 1D with colony formation assay data.

claim: GOT2 knockdown decreased relative abundances of aspartate in PaTu-8902 and MIAPaCa-2 cells.
source: Relative abundances of Asp and αKG in PaTu-8902 (left) and MIAPaCa-2 (right) ishGOT2.1 −Dox (n=3) or +Dox (n=3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1E with metabolomics data.

claim: GOT2 knockdown decreased relative abundances of α-ketoglutarate in PaTu-8902 and MIAPaCa-2 cells.
source: Relative abundances of Asp and αKG in PaTu-8902 (left) and MIAPaCa-2 (right) ishGOT2.1 −Dox (n=3) or +Dox (n=3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1E with metabolomics data.

claim: Supplementation with aspartate and dimethyl-α-ketoglutarate rescued proliferation of GOT2 KD cells.
source: Relative proliferation of PaTu-8902 (left) and MIAPaCa-2 (right) ishGOT2.1 −Dox (n=3) or +Dox (n=3) cultured in normal media (Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium, DMEM) or supplemented with 20 mM Asp and 1 mM dimethyl-αKG (dmαKG).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1F with proliferation assay data.

claim: GOT2 knockdown was specific for GOT2 relative to the cytosolic aspartate aminotransaminase GOT1.
source: This knockdown (KD) was specific for GOT2, relative to the cytosolic aspartate aminotransaminase GOT1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B with western blot data.

claim: GOT2 is not required for the proliferation of non-transformed pancreatic cell types.
source: Consistent with our previous report (Son et al., 2013), GOT2 was not required for the proliferation of non-transformed pancreatic cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F with proliferation data for hPSC and HPNE cells.

claim: GOT2 KD induced numerous changes in the intracellular metabolome of PDA cells.
source: Numerous changes in the intracellular metabolome of GOT2 KD cells were observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B with metabolomics heatmaps and pathway analysis.

claim: Supraphysiological levels of aspartate led to an increase in intracellular aspartate in PDA cells.
source: While these PDAC cell lines do not express Asp transporters, we confirmed that supraphysiological levels of Asp (20-fold excess) led to an increase in intracellular Asp (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C with metabolomics data.

claim: GOT2 KD resulted in a disruption in TCA cycle intermediates.
source: In addition to reduced αKG, there was a disruption in tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle intermediates, consistent with a role for GOT2 in facilitating glutamine anaplerosis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D with metabolomics data.

claim: GOT2 KD impaired glycolysis with a node at glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase, indicative of NADH reductive stress.
source: Aside from the expected decrease in Asp and αKG, and the perturbation of the TCA cycle, closer examination of the GOT2 KD metabolomics dataset revealed an impairment in glycolysis with a node at glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH), indicative of NADH reductive stress (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and illustrated in Figure 2A with a schematic and metabolomics data.

claim: Glycolysis was impaired in GOT2 KD cells as confirmed by Seahorse Flux Analysis.
source: Examination of glycolytic rate via Seahorse Flux Analysis confirmed that glycolysis was indeed impaired in GOT2 KD cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A with Seahorse data.

claim: GAPDH reduces NAD+ to produce NADH, where a buildup of NADH product inhibits GAPDH activity.
source: The GAPDH reduces NAD+ to produce NADH, where a buildup of NADH product inhibits GAPDH activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results and represents established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Metabolite pools in upstream glycolysis and branch pathways like the pentose phosphate pathway are increased in GOT2 KD cells.
source: Indeed, metabolite pools in upstream glycolysis and branch pathways like the pentose phosphate pathway are increased, and those in downstream glycolysis are decreased (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B with metabolomics data.

claim: Metabolite pools in downstream glycolysis are decreased in GOT2 KD cells.
source: Indeed, metabolite pools in upstream glycolysis and branch pathways like the pentose phosphate pathway are increased, and those in downstream glycolysis are decreased (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B with metabolomics data.

claim: In cultured PDA cells, the MAS transfers glycolytic reducing potential to drive the electron transport chain and support the maintenance of cytosolic redox balance.
source: In cultured PDA cells, the MAS transfers glycolytic reducing potential to drive the electron transport chain (ETC) and support the maintenance of cytosolic redox balance (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: GOT2 KD interrupted the malate-aspartate shuttle, preventing the proper transfer of electron potential in the form of NADH between the cytosol and mitochondria.
source: We thus hypothesized that GOT2 KD interrupted this shuttle, preventing the proper transfer of electron potential in the form of NADH between these two compartments.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis in the results based on the observed metabolic changes.

claim: GOT2 KD increased the intracellular ratio of NADH to NAD+.
source: In support of this, GOT2 KD increased the intracellular ratio of NADH to NAD+ (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C with NADH/NAD+ ratio measurements.

claim: NADH accumulation leads to reductive stress, which can be relieved if the cell has access to electron acceptors.
source: NADH accumulation leads to reductive stress, which can be relieved if the cell has access to electron acceptors (Gui et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation.

claim: Pyruvate can accept electrons from NADH, producing lactate and regenerating NAD+, in a reaction catalyzed by lactate dehydrogenase.
source: Pyruvate is a notable metabolite in this regard, as it can accept electrons from NADH, producing lactate and regenerating NAD+, in a reaction catalyzed by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH).
evidence: This is stated in the results and represents established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Culturing GOT2 KD cells in pyruvate rescued proliferation in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Indeed, culturing GOT2 KD cells in pyruvate rescued proliferation in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2D and E; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 2D, 2E, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B with colony formation and proliferation data.

claim: ATP levels dropped with GOT2 KD and were restored with pyruvate supplementation.
source: Additionally, cells expressing a genetically encoded, fluorescent ATP sensor indicated that ATP levels dropped with GOT2 KD and were restored with pyruvate supplementation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), reflecting the link between TCA cycle activity, respiration, and oxidative phosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C with ATP sensor data.

claim: GOT2 knockout impaired colony formation of PDA cells, which was restored through extracellular pyruvate supplementation.
source: In support of the data generated using the doxycycline-inducible shRNA, GOT2 KO impaired colony formation of PDA cells, which was similarly restored through extracellular pyruvate supplementation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F with colony formation data.

claim: α-ketobutyrate is an electron acceptor that turns over NADH in a mechanism analogous to pyruvate but without entering downstream metabolism in the same fashion as pyruvate.
source: The α-ketobutyrate (αKB) is another electron acceptor that turns over NADH in a mechanism analogous to pyruvate but without entering downstream metabolism in the same fashion as pyruvate (Sullivan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation.

claim: α-ketobutyrate rescued proliferation after GOT2 KD.
source: The αKB also rescued proliferation after GOT2 KD (Figure 2F; Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F with proliferation data.

claim: The rescue mechanism is dependent on NADH turnover and not NAD+ synthesis, as the NAD+ precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide failed to rescue GOT2 KD.
source: This mechanism is dependent on NADH turnover and not NAD+ synthesis, as the NAD+ precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) failed to rescue GOT2 KD (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G with colony formation data.

claim: Cytosolic LbNOX, but not mitochondrial LbNOX, rescued proliferation of GOT2 KD cells.
source: Cytosolic LbNOX, but not mitochondrial LbNOX (mLbNOX), rescued proliferation of GOT2 KD cells (Figure 2G; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B with proliferation data.

claim: Mitochondrial LbNOX construct encoded a functional enzyme as defects in proliferation incurred by treatment with complex I inhibitor piericidin could be rescued with mLbNOX.
source: We confirmed the mLbNOX construct encoded a functional enzyme as defects in proliferation incurred by treatment with complex I inhibitor piericidin could be rescued with mLbNOX as reported previously (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C; Titov et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C with proliferation data, supported by citation.

claim: LbNOX reversed the increased NADH/NAD+ ratio induced by GOT2 KD via an overall decrease in NADH levels.
source: LbNOX reversed the increased NADH/NAD+ ratio induced by GOT2 KD via an overall decrease in NADH levels (Figure 2H; Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D with NADH/NAD+ ratio data.

claim: The secreted pyruvate/lactate ratios in the media of LbNOX-expressing cells dramatically increased, indicating a resolution of the cytosolic NADH stress induced by GOT2 KD.
source: Furthermore, the secreted pyruvate/lactate ratios in the media of LbNOX-expressing cells dramatically increased, indicating a resolution of the cytosolic NADH stress induced by GOT2 KD (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F with metabolite measurements.

claim: The metabolic defects observed following GOT2 KD were ameliorated by cytosolic LbNOX activity.
source: Moreover, the metabolic defects observed following GOT2 KD were ameliorated by cytosolic LbNOX activity, including an increase in Asp and αKG, normalization of TCA cycle metabolites, and the release of the glycolytic block at GAPDH (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2G with metabolomics data.

claim: KD of mitochondrial GOT2 could be rescued by balancing the cytosolic NADH/NAD+ pool.
source: The spatial control of the LbNOX system indicated that KD of mitochondrial GOT2 could be rescued by balancing the cytosolic NADH/NAD+ pool.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the LbNOX experiments.

claim: Roughly 50% of the intracellular pyruvate was labeled in U13C-pyruvate tracing experiments.
source: In this experiment, roughly 50% of the intracellular pyruvate was labeled (Figure 2J), in line with the other half of the unlabeled pyruvate coming from glucose, and most of the labeled pyruvate was converted to lactate (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2J with isotope tracing data.

claim: Most of the labeled pyruvate was converted to lactate in U13C-pyruvate tracing experiments.
source: In this experiment, roughly 50% of the intracellular pyruvate was labeled (Figure 2J), in line with the other half of the unlabeled pyruvate coming from glucose, and most of the labeled pyruvate was converted to lactate (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2K with isotope tracing data.

claim: Modest labeling of citrate, aspartate, and alanine from pyruvate was observed.
source: We observed modest labeling of citrate, Asp, and alanine from pyruvate (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B-D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B-D with isotope tracing data.

claim: Labeled TCA cycle and branching pathway intermediates decreased dramatically with UK5099 (MPC inhibitor).
source: While the labeled TCA cycle and branching pathway intermediates decreased dramatically with UK5099, this MPC inhibition had no effect on the pyruvate GOT2 KD rescue phenotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3E with isotope tracing and proliferation data.

claim: MPC inhibition had no effect on the pyruvate GOT2 KD rescue phenotype.
source: While the labeled TCA cycle and branching pathway intermediates decreased dramatically with UK5099, this MPC inhibition had no effect on the pyruvate GOT2 KD rescue phenotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3E with proliferation data.

claim: Supplementation with exogenous lactate, alanine, or nucleoside bases failed to rescue GOT2 KD.
source: Both lactate and alanine can fuel oxidation via the TCA cycle (Hui et al., 2017; Sousa et al., 2016), and Asp is critical for nucleotide production. Pyruvate can be converted into all three of these metabolites, yet supplementation with exogenous lactate, alanine, or nucleoside bases failed to rescue GOT2 KD (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F-H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3F-H with colony formation data.

claim: Pyruvate-mediated rescue of GOT2 KD has a redox role, as opposed to entering the mitochondria for ATP production or biosynthesis.
source: These data collectively suggest a redox role for pyruvate-mediated rescue of GOT2 KD, as opposed to entering the mitochondria for ATP production or biosynthesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the pyruvate tracing and rescue experiments.

claim: GOT2 KD results in accumulation of NADH pools and reductive stress in PDA cells.
source: These findings provide clear evidence using several orthogonal strategies that GOT2 KD results in accumulation of NADH pools and reductive stress in PDA cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary of the findings.

claim: PDA tumors from five different cell lines grew unimpeded with GOT2 KD in vivo.
source: Surprisingly, despite the inhibitory in vitro phenotype, and robust suppression of GOT2 expression in vivo, PDA tumors from five different cell lines grew unimpeded with GOT2 KD (Figure 3A and B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A, 3B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B with tumor volume data and western blots.

claim: Tumors lacking GOT2 were proliferative and displayed a modest but significant increase in Ki67-positive nuclei.
source: Nuclear Ki67 staining confirmed that tumors lacking GOT2 were proliferative and actually displayed a modest, but significant, increase in Ki67-positive nuclei (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C and 3D with immunohistochemistry data.

claim: GOT2 KD had no effect on the growth of orthotopic tumors.
source: Similar to the flank model, GOT2 KD had no effect on the growth of orthotopic tumors (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C with bioluminescence data.

claim: Aspartate abundance was significantly decreased in GOT2 KD tumors.
source: Asp abundance was significantly decreased, yet αKG levels remained constant (Figure 3E), and TCA cycle intermediates were unaffected (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3E with metabolomics data.

claim: α-ketoglutarate levels remained constant in GOT2 KD tumors.
source: Asp abundance was significantly decreased, yet αKG levels remained constant (Figure 3E), and TCA cycle intermediates were unaffected (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3E with metabolomics data.

claim: TCA cycle intermediates were unaffected in GOT2 KD tumors.
source: Asp abundance was significantly decreased, yet αKG levels remained constant (Figure 3E), and TCA cycle intermediates were unaffected (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F with metabolomics data.

claim: A compensatory increase in expression of other αKG-producing enzymes was not observed in GOT2 KD tumors.
source: However, upon examination of the expression of other αKG-producing enzymes in GOT2 KD tumors, we did not observe a compensatory increase in expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G with western blot data.

claim: The glycolytic signature indicative of NADH stress was not observed in the metabolomics analysis from flank GOT2 KD tumors.
source: Finally, the glycolytic signature indicative of NADH stress was not observed in the metabolomics analysis from flank GOT2 KD tumors, further illustrating the differential dependence on GOT2 in PDA in vitro and in vivo (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3F with metabolomics data.

claim: Loss of Got2 had no observable effect on the architecture of the healthy, non-transformed pancreas.
source: Loss of Got2 had no observable effect on the architecture of the healthy, non-transformed pancreas (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C with histology and pancreas weight data.

claim: KC-Got2 mice had a significantly greater percentage of healthy acinar cells compared to KC controls at 3 months.
source: Scoring the hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained tissues from these groups by a blinded pathologist revealed that KC-Got2 mice had a significantly greater percentage of healthy acinar cells compared to KC controls (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4D and 4E with histology and quantification data.

claim: No differences were observed in the percentages of acinar-ductal metaplasia or pancreatic intraepithelial grade between KC-Got2 and KC mice at 3 months.
source: However, no differences were observed in the percentages of acinar-ductal metaplasia or pancreatic intraepithelial grade between KC-Got2 and KC mice (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4E with quantification data.

claim: A slight decrease in weight for KC-Got2 pancreata was observed at 6 months.
source: Additionally, we aged KC-Got2 mice to 6 months and compared the pancreata to matched 6-month KC historic controls, observing a slight decrease in weight for KC-Got2 pancreatic (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4F and 4G with histology and pancreas weight data.

claim: A histological analysis did not identify a difference in number or severity of lesions between KC-Got2 and KC mice at 6 months.
source: A histological analysis by a blinded pathologist did not identify a difference in number or severity of lesions (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4H with quantification data.

claim: Both KC and KC-Got2 mice had progressed to carcinoma after aging for 1 year.
source: In addition, both KC and KC-Got2 mice had progressed to carcinoma after aging for 1 year (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4I and 4J with histology and quantification data.

claim: Loss of Got2 does not affect the progression of PDA following transformation by oncogenic Kras.
source: This suggests that loss of Got2 does not affect the progression of PDA following transformation by oncogenic Kras.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the KC-Got2 mouse model data.

claim: Activated mouse fibroblasts comprised a substantial portion of the microenvironment in tumors regardless of GOT2 status.
source: While the flank tumor milieu in immunocompromised mice is less complex than that of a human PDA tumor, α-smooth muscle actin (αSMA) staining revealed that activated mouse fibroblasts comprised a substantial portion of the microenvironment in tumors regardless of GOT2 status (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A with immunohistochemistry data.

claim: hCAF CM promoted colony formation in PDA cells with GOT2 KD in a dose-dependent manner.
source: In support of our hypothesis, hCAF CM promoted colony formation in PDA cells with GOT2 KD in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 5A and B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A, 5B, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B with colony formation data.

claim: hCAF CM displayed a more pronounced colony formation rescue phenotype compared to CM from tumor-educated macrophages or from PDA cells.
source: Furthermore, hCAF CM displayed a more pronounced colony formation rescue phenotype compared to CM from tumor-educated macrophages (TEMs) or from PDA cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C with colony formation data.

claim: hCAF CM supported colony formation in GOT2 KD cells after being boiled, filtered through a 3 kDa cut-off membrane, or subjected to cycles of freezing and thawing, suggesting the relevant factor(s) was a metabolite.
source: In each of these conditions, hCAF CM supported colony formation in GOT2 KD cells, suggesting the relevant factor(s) was a metabolite (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D with colony formation data.

claim: Pyruvate was one of the most differentially abundant metabolites released by hCAFs into the CM.
source: Interestingly, when the metabolites were ranked in order of relative abundance, compared to the media control, pyruvate was one of the most differentially abundant metabolites released by hCAFs into the CM (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D with metabolomics data.

claim: The absolute concentration of pyruvate in hCAF CM was quantified at 250 µM.
source: Since we used pyruvate-free Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM) to culture hCAFs, to avoid overinterpreting this finding, we quantified the absolute concentration of pyruvate in hCAF CM at 250 µM, with some variability between batches (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5E with absolute quantitation data.

claim: 250 µM pyruvate is a physiologically relevant concentration of pyruvate in serum collected from mice harboring pancreatic tumors.
source: This is a physiologically relevant concentration of pyruvate in serum collected from mice harboring pancreatic tumors (Sullivan et al., 2019), and 250 µM pyruvate rescued GOT2 KD in vitro (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation and reference to Figure 2E.

claim: PDA cells cultured in hCAF CM had elevated levels of intracellular pyruvate.
source: Consistent with the idea of metabolite exchange, PDA cells cultured in hCAF CM had elevated levels of intracellular pyruvate (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F with metabolomics data.

claim: mCAFs isolated from a pancreatic flank xenograft secreted pyruvate at similar levels to hCAFs in vitro.
source: The mCAFs isolated from a pancreatic flank xenograft in an NSG mouse also secreted pyruvate at similar levels to hCAFs in vitro (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5E with absolute quantitation data.

claim: mCAF CM promoted PDA colony formation following GOT2 KD.
source: Furthermore, mCAF CM promoted PDA colony formation following GOT2 KD (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G with colony formation data.

claim: The pyruvate released by CAFs was produced from glucose.
source: To better understand the production and release of pyruvate in CAFs, we traced glucose metabolism using uniformly carbon-labeled (U13C) glucose and LC-MS metabolomics. We demonstrate that the pyruvate released by CAFs was produced from glucose (Figure 5G), and, in support of previous studies (Zhang et al., 2015; Lemons et al., 2010), these CAFs displayed labeling patterns indicative of glycolytic metabolism (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5G with isotope tracing data.

claim: CAFs displayed labeling patterns indicative of glycolytic metabolism.
source: To better understand the production and release of pyruvate in CAFs, we traced glucose metabolism using uniformly carbon-labeled (U13C) glucose and LC-MS metabolomics. We demonstrate that the pyruvate released by CAFs was produced from glucose (Figure 5G), and, in support of previous studies (Zhang et al., 2015; Lemons et al., 2010), these CAFs displayed labeling patterns indicative of glycolytic metabolism (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5H with isotope tracing data, supported by citations.

claim: Aspartate was quantified at 15 µM in CAF CM.
source: However, we quantified Asp at 15 µM and αKG at 50 µM in CAF CM (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), well below the reported values from mouse serum (Sullivan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A with absolute quantitation data.

claim: α-ketoglutarate was quantified at 50 µM in CAF CM.
source: However, we quantified Asp at 15 µM and αKG at 50 µM in CAF CM (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), well below the reported values from mouse serum (Sullivan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A with absolute quantitation data.

claim: Pyruvate rescued proliferation of GOT2 KD to a greater extent than the combination of aspartate and α-ketoglutarate.
source: Nevertheless, we tested the rescue activity of reported serum levels of Asp and αKG (50 µM and 500 µM, respectively; Sullivan et al., 2019), again utilizing the dimethyl-αKG and compared this to serum levels of pyruvate (250 µM). Here we found that pyruvate rescued proliferation of GOT2 KD to a greater extent than the combination of Asp and αKG (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B with proliferation data.

claim: Pyruvate, and not aspartate or α-ketoglutarate, is responsible for the GOT2 KD rescue activity of CAF CM in vitro.
source: Therefore, we conclude that pyruvate, and not Asp or αKG, is responsible for the GOT2 KD rescue activity of CAF CM in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion based on the metabolite quantitation and rescue experiments.

claim: Both hCAF CM and extracellular pyruvate conferred resistance to PDA cells against the complex I inhibitors rotenone, phenformin, and IACS-010759.
source: Indeed, both hCAF CM and extracellular pyruvate conferred resistance to PDA cells against the complex I inhibitors rotenone, phenformin, and IACS-010759 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C; Molina et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C with viability data.

claim: PDA cell lines primarily express MCT1 and MCT4.
source: Pyruvate can be transported by four monocarboxylate transporter (MCT) isoforms (Halestrap, 2013; Halestrap, 2012a; Halestrap and Wilson, 2012b), and an analysis of the CCLE database suggests that PDA cell lines primarily express MCT1 and MCT4 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A with CCLE expression data.

claim: MCT1 has a higher affinity for pyruvate than MCT4.
source: Since MCT1 has a higher affinity for pyruvate than MCT4 (Halestrap, 2012a), we decided to focus on MCT1 as the transporter by which PDA cells import pyruvate (Rao et al., 2020; Rao et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation.

claim: PDA cells express significantly higher levels of MCT1 compared to hCAFs.
source: Indeed, PDA cells express significantly higher levels of MCT1, as compared to hCAFs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B with western blot data.

claim: PDA cells express high levels of MCT1 in a murine syngeneic orthotopic pancreatic tumor.
source: Similarly, examining expression of MCT1 from a recently published single-cell analysis of a murine syngeneic orthotopic pancreatic tumor (Steele et al., 2020) indicated that PDA cells express high levels of MCT1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C with single-cell RNA sequencing data, supported by citation.

claim: The pyruvate/lactate ratios mimicking CAF CM, serum, or TIF promoted the growth of GOT2 KD cells in vitro.
source: When the measured pyruvate and lactate levels from each of these permutations were added back to regular media, the pyruvate/lactate ratios mimicking CAF CM, serum, or TIF promoted the growth of GOT2 KD cells in vitro (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6C with proliferation data.

claim: The pyruvate/lactate ratios in CAF CM in vitro and in the in vivo TME are favorable for pyruvate import, possibly through MCT1.
source: These data indicate the pyruvate/lactate ratios in CAF CM in vitro and in the in vivo TME are favorable for pyruvate import, possibly through MCT1.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the pyruvate/lactate ratio data.

claim: MCT1 chemical inhibition reduced the pyruvate and hCAF CM rescue of GOT2 KD.
source: In support of our hypothesis, MCT1 chemical inhibition reduced the pyruvate and hCAF CM rescue of GOT2 KD (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6D with colony formation data.

claim: MCT1 KD modestly slowed the growth of GOT2 KD cells cultured in pyruvate or hCAF CM.
source: MCT1 KD modestly slowed the growth of GOT2 KD cells cultured in pyruvate or hCAF CM (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,G with proliferation data.

claim: MCT1 KO in GOT2 KD cells blocked pyruvate rescue.
source: Indeed, MCT1 KO in GOT2 KD cells blocked pyruvate rescue (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6F with colony formation data.

claim: MCT1 inhibition was most effective at physiological levels of pyruvate (250 µM).
source: We also demonstrate that MCT1 inhibition was most effective at physiological levels of pyruvate (250 µM; Figure 6F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H with colony formation data.

claim: MCT1 KO cells cultured with U13C-pyruvate demonstrated reduced uptake of pyruvate.
source: Furthermore, MCT1 KO cells cultured with U13C-pyruvate demonstrated reduced uptake of pyruvate, as measured by intracellular labeled pyruvate (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6G with isotope tracing data.

claim: Reduced pyruvate uptake in MCT1 KO cells was observed more clearly in dramatically reduced levels of labeled lactate.
source: Since pyruvate is rapidly imported and converted to lactate, the reduced pyruvate uptake was observed more clearly in dramatically reduced levels of labeled lactate in MCT1 KO cells (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6G with isotope tracing data.

claim: AZD3965 reversed the rescue activity of pyruvate or hCAF CM in PDA cells treated with IACS-010759.
source: The AZD3965 also reversed the rescue activity of pyruvate or hCAF CM in PDA cells treated with IACS-010759 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1I with viability data.

claim: PDA cell lines highly expressed the LDHA isoform of LDH.
source: Our PDA cell lines highly expressed the LDHA isoform of LDH, as determined by western blotting (Figure 6—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1J with western blot data.

claim: Inhibiting LDHA with FX11 slowed the in vitro proliferation of GOT2 KD cells cultured in pyruvate or hCAF CM.
source: In further support of our model, inhibiting LDHA with FX11 slowed the in vitro proliferation of GOT2 KD cells cultured in pyruvate or hCAF CM, relative to single agent controls (Figure 6H, Figure 6—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1K with proliferation data.

claim: Perturbation of mitochondrial metabolism with GOT2 KD or complex I inhibition disrupts redox balance in PDA cells, which can be restored through import of pyruvate from the extracellular environment and reduction to lactate to regenerate NAD+.
source: Cumulatively, these data support an in vitro model whereby perturbation of mitochondrial metabolism with GOT2 KD or complex I inhibition disrupts redox balance in PDA cells. This can be restored through import of pyruvate from the extracellular environment and reduction to lactate to regenerate NAD+.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary of the in vitro findings.

claim: MCT1 KD had no effect on the growth of GOT2 KD subcutaneous xenografts.
source: In vitro, MCT1 KD had a modest effect on the proliferation of GOT2 KD cells cultured in pyruvate or hCAF CM. In contrast, we found that MCT1 KD had no effect on the growth of GOT2 KD subcutaneous xenografts (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B with tumor volume data.

claim: MCT1 KO did not impact the growth of GOT2 KD tumors in vivo.
source: However, MCT1 KO similarly did not impact the growth of GOT2 KD tumors in vivo, which is in stark contrast to the results observed in vitro whereby MCT1 KO blocked the rescue of colony formation in GOT2 KD cells by pyruvate (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E with tumor volume data.

claim: MCT1 was not detectable at endpoint in MCT1 KO xenografts.
source: In these tumors, MCT1 was not detectable at endpoint and we did not observe a compensatory increase in MCT4 expression in either cell lines or xenografts with MCT1 KO (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2F,G with western blot data.

claim: A compensatory increase in MCT4 expression was not observed in cell lines or xenografts with MCT1 KO.
source: In these tumors, MCT1 was not detectable at endpoint and we did not observe a compensatory increase in MCT4 expression in either cell lines or xenografts with MCT1 KO (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2F,G with western blot data.

claim: Administration of AZD3965 did not impact the growth of GOT2 KD xenografts.
source: Similarly, administration of AZD3965 did not impact the growth of GOT2 KD xenografts, again contrasting our in vitro data showing strong blockade of GOT2 KD rescue by pyruvate or hCAF CM with MCT1 chemical inhibition (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E-G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2H with tumor volume data.

claim: FX11 had no effect on GOT2 KD growth in vivo.
source: Lastly, unlike in vitro, FX11 had no effect on GOT2 KD growth in vivo (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B with tumor volume data.

claim: KD of GOT2 in vitro disrupts the MAS and renders PDA cells incapable of transferring reducing equivalents between the cytosol and mitochondria, leading to a cytosolic accumulation of NADH.
source: KD of GOT2 in vitro disrupts the MAS and renders PDA cells incapable of transferring reducing equivalents between the cytosol and mitochondria, leading to a cytosolic accumulation of NADH.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: NADH accumulation from GOT2 KD predominantly impacts the rate of glycolysis, an NAD+-coupled pathway, with secondary impacts on mitochondrial metabolism that together slow the proliferation of PDA cells in vitro.
source: This predominantly impacts the rate of glycolysis, an NAD+-coupled pathway, with secondary impacts on mitochondrial metabolism that together slow the proliferation of PDA cells in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: GOT2 feeds into the ME1 shunt, which produces pyruvate and sustains intracellular NADPH levels.
source: For instance, GOT2 feeds into the ME1 shunt, which we demonstrated previously also produces pyruvate and sustains intracellular NADPH levels (Son et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Pyruvate is present in mouse serum at 250 µM.
source: Indeed, pyruvate is present in mouse serum at 250 µM (Sullivan et al., 2019), a concentration which is sufficient to compensate for GOT2 KD in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Pancreatic CAFs release pyruvate in vitro, which can be utilized by PDA cells.
source: Furthermore, we also demonstrate that pancreatic CAFs release pyruvate in vitro, which can be utilized by PDA cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: CAFs from other cancers release pyruvate.
source: This is supported by previous findings in CAFs from other cancers (Sakamoto et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Glutaminase inhibition was ineffective in vivo in KRAS-driven non-small cell lung cancer models as lung tumors primarily utilized glucose as a carbon source for the TCA cycle instead of glutamine.
source: First, previous work in KRAS*-driven non-small cell lung cancer reported differential dependencies on glutaminolysis in vitro in cell lines versus in vivo in lung tumors. Glutaminase inhibition was ineffective in vivo in these models as lung tumors primarily utilized glucose as a carbon source for the TCA cycle instead of glutamine.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a potential explanation for the in vivo findings, though no specific citation is provided.

claim: MCT4 has a lower affinity for pyruvate than MCT1 but can transport pyruvate.
source: Second, while MCT4 has a lower affinity for pyruvate than MCT1, it can transport pyruvate (Halestrap, 2012a).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: MCT4 has been shown to confer resistance to cancer cells against MCT1 inhibition.
source: It is also highly expressed in the cell lines used here (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F,G) and has been shown to confer resistance to cancer cells against MCT1 inhibition (Bonglack et al., 2021; Hong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations and reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2F,G.

claim: PDA cells could obtain pyruvate through macropinocytosis even with sufficient MCT blockade.
source: Third, even with sufficient MCT blockade, PDA cells could still obtain pyruvate through other processes, such as macropinocytosis (Kamphorst et al., 2015; Commisso et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a potential explanation and supported by citations.

claim: Numerous circulating metabolites can function as electron acceptors and could relieve the intracellular accumulation of NADH if cancer cells are unable to import pyruvate.
source: Fourth, while our study focuses on pyruvate, numerous circulating metabolites can function as electron acceptors and could relieve the intracellular accumulation of NADH if cancer cells are unable to import pyruvate (Hui et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a potential explanation and supported by citation.

claim: Reduction of pyruvate to lactate by LDH is not the only reaction by which NAD+ is regenerated.
source: Fifth, reduction of pyruvate to lactate by LDH is not the only reaction by which NAD+ is regenerated. claim: Redox homeostasis is a vital aspect of cancer cell metabolism and is maintained through a complex web of intracellular compensatory pathways and extracellular interactions.
source: Nevertheless, our data emphasize that redox homeostasis is a vital aspect of cancer cell metabolism and is maintained through a complex web of intracellular compensatory pathways and extracellular interactions.

claim: GOT2 inhibition dramatically decreases aspartate levels both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Aside from its broader role in redox balance, GOT2 is also a prominent source of Asp in PDA cells, and we demonstrate that GOT2 inhibition dramatically decreases Asp levels both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Aspartate availability is rate limiting in rapidly proliferating cells.
source: Previous studies have shown that Asp availability is rate limiting in rapidly proliferating cells (Sullivan et al., 2015; Birsoy et al., 2015; Sullivan et al., 2018; Garcia-Bermudez et al., 2018).

claim: Free aspartate is available at low micromolar concentrations and has limited uptake capacity in PDA cells.
source: Additionally, free Asp is available at low micromolar concentrations and has limited uptake capacity of PDA cells (Sullivan et al., 2019).

claim: Pyruvate regenerates NAD+ allowing broader metabolic processes to resume, including aspartate production and nucleotide biosynthesis.

evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: CAFs engage in cooperative metabolic crosstalk with cancer cells in many different tumor types.
source: Recent studies have shown that CAFs engage in cooperative metabolic crosstalk with cancer cells in many different tumor types (Lyssiotis and Kimmelman, 2017; Sousa et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2016; Sanford-Crane et al., 2019; Schwörer et al., 2019).

claim: Some types of activated fibroblasts are known to be highly glycolytic.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing in murine and human pancreatic tumor models has led to a recent appreciation for the heterogeneity of CAFs.
source: Yet the advent of single-cell RNA sequencing in murine and human pancreatic tumor models has led to a recent appreciation for the heterogeneity of CAFs (Elyada et al., 2019; Ohlund et al., 2017; Neuzillet et al., 2019; Hosein et al., 2019; Helms et al., 2022; Hutton et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The newly identified iCAF, myCAF, and apCAF populations have distinct functions in a pancreatic tumor.
source: The newly identified iCAF, myCAF, and apCAF populations have distinct functions in a pancreatic tumor (Elyada et al., 2019) and likely employ distinct metabolism to carry out these functions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Disrupting the MAS shuttle via GOT2 KD or blocking complex I with small molecule inhibitors were less effective in vitro when PDA cells were cultured in supplemental pyruvate or CAF CM.
source: Indeed, approaches like disrupting the MAS shuttle via GOT2 KD or blocking complex I with small molecule inhibitors were less effective in vitro when PDA cells were cultured in supplemental pyruvate or CAF CM.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Numerous mitochondrial inhibitors are currently in clinical trials against solid tumor types.
source: These data are relevant since numerous mitochondrial inhibitors are currently in clinical trials against solid tumor types (NCT03291938, NCT03026517, NCT03699319, and NCT02071862).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with clinical trial identifiers.

claim: Complex I inhibitors are more effective in combination with AZD3965, a selective inhibitor of MCT1.

evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: The abundance of CAFs present in a tumor, as well as the level of circulating pyruvate in the patient, could predict outcomes for treatment with metabolic therapies that lead to redox imbalance.
source: Furthermore, the abundance of CAFs present in a tumor, as well as the level of circulating pyruvate in the patient, could predict outcomes for treatment with metabolic therapies that lead to redox imbalance.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation based on the findings.

claim: A more detailed understanding of the metabolic crosstalk occurring in a pancreatic tumor can shed light on potential resistance mechanisms and inform more effective metabolic therapies.
source: Targeting pancreatic cancer metabolism is an alluring approach, and a more detailed understanding of the metabolic crosstalk occurring in a pancreatic tumor can shed light on potential resistance mechanisms and inform more effective metabolic therapies.
